cards.front: Recall a key point about Fiscal Policy
cards.back: Fiscal policy uses government spending and taxation to influence the economy. Expansionary: increase spending/cut taxes to boost demand. Contractionary: cut spending/raise taxes to reduce demand.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fiscal Policy
cards.back: Expansionary fiscal policy can achieve growth and reduce unemployment but may cause inflation and increase the budget deficit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fiscal Policy
cards.back: A budget deficit (spending > revenue) increases national debt; a surplus (revenue > spending) reduces it. The UK has run deficits for most of the last 50 years.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fiscal Policy
cards.back: Fiscal policy can redistribute income (progressive taxes, welfare spending) and correct market failures (public goods, taxing externalities).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Fiscal Policy
cards.back: Limitations: time lags (decisions take time to implement), crowding out (government borrowing may push up interest rates), and political constraints.

cards.front: What should you know about economics exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating fiscal policy, use the TAL framework: Timing (will it take effect when needed?), Accuracy (will the right amount be spent?), Long-term effects (debt consequences?).
